costNote: Gallagher is a people business, so pay is its direct cost of service: $2,237M across producers, brokers and service staff (55% of revenue, before reimbursements). The AssuredPartners acquisition — the largest in company history — added thousands of employees.

opex.name: Operating expenses
opex.note: Offices, technology and travel across the global network.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Writing down the value of the hundreds of agencies Gallagher has acquired — a permanent feature of its roll-up model.

opex.name: Reimbursements & earnout changes
opex.note: $46M of client costs billed back (they also appear in revenue, so they wash) plus $16M of revised estimates for acquisition earnout payments.

footerNote: Gallagher reports three segments and no consolidated cost-of-revenue line; compensation is treated here as the direct cost of service, consistent with a people business. Consolidated figures are the sum of the Brokerage, Risk Management and Corporate segment statements in the release (revenue includes $46M of reimbursements, which also appear in expenses). Net earnings of $406M were $403M attributable to controlling interests.

oneTimers.label: AssuredPartners integration
oneTimers.text: Gallagher closed AssuredPartners — the largest acquisition in its history — and the quarter carries acquisition integration costs (a $103M pretax adjustment item in Brokerage) plus elevated amortization. Adjusted EPS of $3.00 strips these out; GAAP was $1.55.

segments.name: Brokerage
segments.note: Insurance brokerage — commissions and fees of $3,473M, up 19% reported with 5% organic growth. Segment net earnings $515M; adjusted EBITDAC $1,222M.

segments.name: Risk Management
segments.note: Claims handling and risk services for clients (third-party administration) — $457M of fees plus $46M of reimbursements. Segment net earnings $61M.

sources.label: Gallagher Q3 2026 earnings release — SEC EDGAR Ex-99.1 (8-K, Oct 29, 2026)

takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDAC grew 25% — the 26th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth — with margins still expanding. Brokerage organic growth was 5%.
takeaways.title: The streak continues

takeaways.text: GAAP EPS of $1.55 is barely half the adjusted $3.00: the gap is amortization ($212M after tax effect in adjustments), AssuredPartners integration and workforce/lease charges. Investors pay for the adjusted number; the GAAP one funds the roll-up.
takeaways.title: GAAP vs adjusted is the whole debate

takeaways.text: The Corporate segment lost $170M — mostly $168M of interest on acquisition debt. It is the carrying cost of the roll-up model.
takeaways.title: Corporate drag is the debt bill

verdict: The roll-up rolls on: revenue +18%, adjusted profit +25% — while GAAP EPS of $1.55 shows what the acquisition machine costs.
